lastRunAt.description: When the detection engine last read the tenant's audit trail.

tenantId.description: The target tenant: the tenant of the role.

requireMfa.description: The source session must be MFA-verified (default true).

externalId.description: A shared secret the caller must present on `roles.assume`; only its SHA-256 is stored.

passSourceAttributes.description: Pass the source identity's attributes into role sessions (default: only for same-tenant trusts).

allowedTagKeys.description: Session tag keys callers may set (at most 50), or exactly ['*']; default none.

sourceIdentityMode.description: Whether callers may or must state a source identity; default 'forbidden'.

tenantId.description: The tenant of the role, the provider and the service account.

providerId.description: The OIDC provider whose tokens the trust admits (in the same tenant).

serviceAccountId.description: The active service account sessions act as (stored as `sourceIdentityId`).

conditions.description:
Claim conditions: a policy statement's `conditions` block over `token.<claim>` keys (at most 20 entries). It must
pin `token.sub` with StringEquals, or StringLike with any wildcard only after two complete segments such as
`repo:acme/*` (else WEAK_TRUST_CONDITIONS).

tagClaims.description: Session tag key to flattened claim name (`token.<claim>`), at most 10.

sourceIdentityClaim.description: The flattened claim that becomes the session's source identity; a token without a valid one is refused.

passSourceAttributes.description: Pass the service account's attributes into role sessions (default true).

requiresExternalId.description: The caller must present an external ID.

verified.description: Whether the signature, issuer, audience and time claims verified against the provider.

reason.description: Set when the exchange would refuse the token.

claims.description: The verified registered claims; `aud` is the provider audience the token was accepted for.

conditions.description: The trust conditions; `failed` lists each unmet entry as `Operator:key`.

sessionTags.description: The session tags the trust's `tagClaims` would map.

sourceIdentity.description: The source identity the trust's `sourceIdentityClaim` would map.

before.description: Epoch milliseconds, no later than now + 1.

deletionAt.description: When a pending deletion becomes final.

stages.description: Stage labels and the version each points at.

due.description: A scheduled rotation is past due.

kmsKeyId.description: The customer-managed key the values are encrypted under.

checkedOut.description: Live check-outs (who holds the value, until when).

exclude.description: Characters never used (a target system that rejects some symbols, say).

eachClass.description: At least one character of each class the charset keeps (lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols).

required.description: The value is handed out only through a check-out (reveal is refused with CHECKOUT_REQUIRED).

exclusive.description: One holder at a time; others get SECRET_CHECKED_OUT until it is checked in or expires.

rotateOnCheckin.description: Rotate the value when a check-out ends, so a returned password stops working.

requireReason.description: A check-out must say why (kept with the lease and in the audit log).

stages.description: Stage labels pointing at this version.

name.description: The claim name in the credential.

selective.description: Holders choose whether to reveal it (default true); false puts it in every presentation.

required.description: Refuse to issue when the value is missing (default false: the claim is left out).

txCode.description: The one-time PIN the wallet asks for, when the offer requires one: give it to the person another way.

ext.description: Whether the key may be exported.

crv.description: EC curve or OKP key pair subtype.

d.description: Private RSA exponent, EC key, or OKP key.

x.description: EC public key X coordinate or OKP public key.

type.description: The credential type, when the issuer is a tenant of this deployment and still has it.

claims.description: Every claim: signed plain claims and the disclosures presented (never `_sd`/`_sd_alg`).

disclosed.description: Names of the claims that came from disclosures.

keyBinding.description: The key-binding JWT's audience, nonce and time, for verifiers that check them themselves.

inScope.description: People the scope matches right now (active people only).

wouldStart.description: People a run would start for at the next evaluation (joiners, due dates), before the daily brake.

upcoming.description: Date triggers: people whose date falls within the next 30 days.

steps.description: Whether the owner may perform each step right now (steps that need no permission are always allowed).

archived.description: Events archived per tenant in this run.

failed.description: Tenants whose chain did not verify or whose sink failed; their cursor did not move.

gaps.description: Sequences deleted before they were archived (pruned without an archive configured).

busy.description: Tenants another run is archiving right now (it holds their lease); they were skipped.

truncated.description: The run stopped at `limit`; run it again to continue.

deviceProof.description:
The unverified device proof the request carried (`x-better-iam-device`, a compact JWS of at most 2048 characters).
Decisions verify it against the registered device keys and the session before it counts; never trust it as is.

kind.description:
`user` (sign-in and impersonation sessions), `api-key` (service-account and agent keys), `role` (assumed roles,
including web-identity sessions), `session-token` (temporary credentials minted from a user session or API key) or
`delegated` (an agent acting on a person's behalf under a delegation; the identity is the person). Code that
branches on the kind must fail closed for kinds it does not know.

agentId.description: Delegated sessions: the agent acting for the session's identity, and the delegation that allows it.

mfaAuthenticatedAt.description:
When a first-hand second factor (TOTP, passkey or an MFA step-up) was last verified for this session; exposed to
policies as principal.mfaTime. Absent on remembered-device, impersonation, API-key, web-identity and legacy rows.

credentialAuthorityId.description: The authority that issued an API key; session tokens minted from the key copy it and are bounded by its ceilings.

sessionName.description: Temporary credentials: a caller-chosen label (/^[\w+=,.@-]{2,64}$/), exposed as principal.sessionName.

sourceIdentity.description: Role sessions: the verified or trust-permitted source identity, exposed as principal.sourceIdentity.

sessionTags.description: Role sessions: per-session tags admitted by the trust, exposed as principal.sessionTags.{key}.

format.description: Temporary credentials issued as IAM-signed session JWTs; the row stores the hash of the JWT like any token.

audience.description: Session JWTs: the audiences the token was issued for.

webIdentity.description: Web-identity role sessions: the OIDC provider and the verified external subject behind the session.

method.description: The sign-in method that established a user session; exposed to policies as principal.authMethod.

name.description: API keys only: an administrator-facing label and purpose (`credentials.create`/`credentials.update`).

impersonatorId.description: The administrator acting through this session (`identities.impersonate`); such sessions end with the administrator's own.

trustedDeviceId.description: Set when a remembered device satisfied the MFA requirement instead of a fresh second factor.

uniqueKey.description: Optional database-enforced natural key, unique within collection and tenant.

broken.description: Invariants that newly failed (or gained violators) since the previous check, audited as `invariant:broken`.

restored.description: Invariants that pass again, audited as `invariant:restored`.

closed.description: Campaigns closed in this run, with how their items ended.

skipped.description: Open auto-closing campaigns that are not due yet.

integrity.description:
The **`integrity`** read-only property of the Request interface contains the subresource integrity value of the request.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request/integrity)

keepalive.description:
The **`keepalive`** read-only property of the Request interface contains the request's `keepalive` setting (`true` or `false`), which indicates whether the browser will keep the associated request alive if the page that initiated it is unloaded before the request is complete.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request/keepalive)

method.description:
The **`method`** read-only property of the `POST`, etc.) A String indicating the method of the request.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request/method)

referrer.description:
The **`referrer`** read-only property of the Request.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request/referrer)

url.description:
The **`url`** read-only property of the Request interface contains the URL of the request.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request/url)

aborted.description:
The **`aborted`** read-only property returns a value that indicates whether the asynchronous operations the signal is communicating with are aborted (`true`) or not (`false`).

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/aborted)

reason.description:
The **`reason`** read-only property returns a JavaScript value that indicates the abort reason.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/reason)

locked.description:
The **`locked`** read-only property of the ReadableStream interface returns whether or not the readable stream is locked to a reader.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/ReadableStream/locked)

ok.description:
The **`ok`** read-only property of the Response interface contains a Boolean stating whether the response was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response/ok)

redirected.description:
The **`redirected`** read-only property of the Response interface indicates whether or not the response is the result of a request you made which was redirected.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected)

status.description:
The **`status`** read-only property of the Response interface contains the HTTP status codes of the response.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response/status)

statusText.description:
The **`statusText`** read-only property of the Response interface contains the status message corresponding to the HTTP status code in Response.status.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response/statusText)

url.description:
The **`url`** read-only property of the Response interface contains the URL of the response.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response/url)

aborted.description:
The `message.aborted` property will be `true` if the request has
been aborted.

httpVersion.description:
In case of server request, the HTTP version sent by the client. In the case of
client response, the HTTP version of the connected-to server.
Probably either `'1.1'` or `'1.0'`.

Also `message.httpVersionMajor` is the first integer and `message.httpVersionMinor` is the second.

rawTrailers.description:
The raw request/response trailer keys and values exactly as they were
received. Only populated at the `'end'` event.

method.description:
**Only valid for request obtained from {@link Server}.**

The request method as a string. Read only. Examples: `'GET'`, `'DELETE'`.

url.description:
**Only valid for request obtained from {@link Server}.**

Request URL string. This contains only the URL that is present in the actual
HTTP request. Take the following request:

```http
GET /status?name=ryan HTTP/1.1
Accept: text/plain
```

To parse the URL into its parts:

```js
new URL(`http://${process.env.HOST ?? 'localhost'}${request.url}`);
```

When `request.url` is `'/status?name=ryan'` and `process.env.HOST` is undefined:

```console
$ node
> new URL(`http://${process.env.HOST ?? 'localhost'}${request.url}`);
URL {
  href: 'http://localhost/status?name=ryan',
  origin: 'http://localhost',
  protocol: 'http:',
  username: '',
  password: '',
  host: 'localhost',
  hostname: 'localhost',
  port: '',
  pathname: '/status',
  search: '?name=ryan',
  searchParams: URLSearchParams { 'name' => 'ryan' },
  hash: ''
}
```

Ensure that you set `process.env.HOST` to the server's host name, or consider replacing this part entirely. If using `req.headers.host`, ensure proper
validation is used, as clients may specify a custom `Host` header.

statusCode.description:
**Only valid for response obtained from {@link ClientRequest}.**

The 3-digit HTTP response status code. E.G. `404`.

statusMessage.description:
**Only valid for response obtained from {@link ClientRequest}.**

The HTTP response status message (reason phrase). E.G. `OK` or `Internal Server Error`.

readableAborted.description: Returns whether the stream was destroyed or errored before emitting `'end'`.

readable.description:
Is `true` if it is safe to call {@link read}, which means
the stream has not been destroyed or emitted `'error'` or `'end'`.

readableEncoding.description: Getter for the property `encoding` of a given `Readable` stream. The `encoding` property can be set using the {@link setEncoding} method.

readableFlowing.description:
This property reflects the current state of a `Readable` stream as described
in the [Three states](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/stream.html#three-states) section.

readableHighWaterMark.description: Returns the value of `highWaterMark` passed when creating this `Readable`.

readableLength.description:
This property contains the number of bytes (or objects) in the queue
ready to be read. The value provides introspection data regarding
the status of the `highWaterMark`.

readableObjectMode.description: Getter for the property `objectMode` of a given `Readable` stream.

errored.description: Returns error if the stream has been destroyed with an error.

autoSelectFamilyAttemptedAddresses.description:
This property is only present if the family autoselection algorithm is enabled in `socket.connect(options)`
and it is an array of the addresses that have been attempted.

Each address is a string in the form of `$IP:$PORT`.
If the connection was successful, then the last address is the one that the socket is currently connected to.

bufferSize.description:
This property shows the number of characters buffered for writing. The buffer
may contain strings whose length after encoding is not yet known. So this number
is only an approximation of the number of bytes in the buffer.

`net.Socket` has the property that `socket.write()` always works. This is to
help users get up and running quickly. The computer cannot always keep up
with the amount of data that is written to a socket. The network connection
simply might be too slow. Node.js will internally queue up the data written to a
socket and send it out over the wire when it is possible.

The consequence of this internal buffering is that memory may grow.
Users who experience large or growing `bufferSize` should attempt to
"throttle" the data flows in their program with `socket.pause()` and `socket.resume()`.

connecting.description:
If `true`, `socket.connect(options[, connectListener])` was
called and has not yet finished. It will stay `true` until the socket becomes
connected, then it is set to `false` and the `'connect'` event is emitted. Note
that the `socket.connect(options[, connectListener])` callback is a listener for the `'connect'` event.

pending.description:
This is `true` if the socket is not connected yet, either because `.connect()`has not yet been called or because it is still in the process of connecting
(see `socket.connecting`).

localAddress.description:
The string representation of the local IP address the remote client is
connecting on. For example, in a server listening on `'0.0.0.0'`, if a client
connects on `'192.168.1.1'`, the value of `socket.localAddress` would be`'192.168.1.1'`.

localPort.description: The numeric representation of the local port. For example, `80` or `21`.

localFamily.description: The string representation of the local IP family. `'IPv4'` or `'IPv6'`.

remoteAddress.description:
The string representation of the remote IP address. For example,`'74.125.127.100'` or `'2001:4860:a005::68'`. Value may be `undefined` if
the socket is destroyed (for example, if the client disconnected).

remoteFamily.description:
The string representation of the remote IP family. `'IPv4'` or `'IPv6'`. Value may be `undefined` if
the socket is destroyed (for example, if the client disconnected).

remotePort.description:
The numeric representation of the remote port. For example, `80` or `21`. Value may be `undefined` if
the socket is destroyed (for example, if the client disconnected).

timeout.description:
The socket timeout in milliseconds as set by `socket.setTimeout()`.
It is `undefined` if a timeout has not been set.

allowHalfOpen.description:
If `false` then the stream will automatically end the writable side when the
readable side ends. Set initially by the `allowHalfOpen` constructor option,
which defaults to `true`.

This can be changed manually to change the half-open behavior of an existing
`Duplex` stream instance, but must be changed before the `'end'` event is emitted.

readable.description:
Is `true` if it is safe to call {@link read}, which means
the stream has not been destroyed or emitted `'error'` or `'end'`.

readableEncoding.description: Getter for the property `encoding` of a given `Readable` stream. The `encoding` property can be set using the {@link setEncoding} method.

readableFlowing.description:
This property reflects the current state of a `Readable` stream as described
in the [Three states](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/stream.html#three-states) section.

readableObjectMode.description: Getter for the property `objectMode` of a given `Readable` stream.

errored.description: Returns error if the stream has been destroyed with an error.

writable.description:
Is `true` if it is safe to call `writable.write()`, which means
the stream has not been destroyed, errored, or ended.

writableAborted.description: Returns whether the stream was destroyed or errored before emitting `'finish'`.

writableEnded.description:
Is `true` after `writable.end()` has been called. This property
does not indicate whether the data has been flushed, for this use `writable.writableFinished` instead.

writableFinished.description: Is set to `true` immediately before the `'finish'` event is emitted.

writableHighWaterMark.description: Return the value of `highWaterMark` passed when creating this `Writable`.

writableLength.description:
This property contains the number of bytes (or objects) in the queue
ready to be written. The value provides introspection data regarding
the status of the `highWaterMark`.

writableObjectMode.description: Getter for the property `objectMode` of a given `Writable` stream.

writableCorked.description:
Number of times `writable.uncork()` needs to be
called in order to fully uncork the stream.

writableNeedDrain.description: Is `true` if the stream's buffer has been full and stream will emit `'drain'`.

statusCode.description:
When using implicit headers (not calling `response.writeHead()` explicitly),
this property controls the status code that will be sent to the client when
the headers get flushed.

```js
response.statusCode = 404;
```

After response header was sent to the client, this property indicates the
status code which was sent out.

statusMessage.description:
When using implicit headers (not calling `response.writeHead()` explicitly),
this property controls the status message that will be sent to the client when
the headers get flushed. If this is left as `undefined` then the standard
message for the status code will be used.

```js
response.statusMessage = 'Not found';
```

After response header was sent to the client, this property indicates the
status message which was sent out.

strictContentLength.description:
If set to `true`, Node.js will check whether the `Content-Length` header value and the size of the body, in bytes, are equal.
Mismatching the `Content-Length` header value will result
in an `Error` being thrown, identified by `code:``'ERR_HTTP_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH'`.

headersSent.description: Read-only. `true` if the headers were sent, otherwise `false`.

socket.description:
Reference to the underlying socket. Usually, users will not want to access
this property.

After calling `outgoingMessage.end()`, this property will be nulled.

Is `true` if it is safe to call `writable.write()`, which means
the stream has not been destroyed, errored, or ended.

type.description: The resource type whose rows are filtered.

expiredIdentities.description: Identities past their scheduled deactivation that the worker disabled in this run.

expiredActivations.description: Ended role activations removed in this run.

expiredMemberships.description: Temporary group memberships past their end removed in this run.

expiredAssignments.description: Access-package assignments past their end removed in this run (their bindings and memberships expire on their own).

dryRun.description: Report what would change without writing anything.

limit.description: Most records examined per collection (a sample, for `selfCheck`); by default all of them.

resealed.description: Values re-sealed with the current secret (or, in a dry run, that would be), per collection.

unreadable.description: Values no configured secret opens, per collection: sealed with a secret that is gone.

current.description: Values already sealed with the current secret.

complete.description: Every record was examined; false when `limit` cut a collection short (the counts are a sample).

done.description:
Nothing sealed with a previous secret remains: the run examined everything and (in a dry run)
found nothing to re-seal. Only then can `previousSecrets` go.

cap.description: Most records counted per backlog check (default 1000); larger backlogs report the cap.

deliveryRetentionMs.description: The `deliveryRetentionMs` your sweep runs with (default 30 days), so its backlog is judged the same way.

graceMs.description: The `graceMs` your sweep runs with (default 5 minutes).

storage.description: The adapter's own view, when it can describe itself.

check.description: Stable identifier, for suppressing or alerting on one check.

count.description: How many records the finding concerns, when it is about stored data (capped at `cap`).

settings.description: Adapter settings worth checking in production (journal mode, durability, size, server version).

sent.description: Tenants whose owners were emailed, with the recipient count and the finding counts.

skipped.description: Tenants left alone: not active, digested within the interval, nothing to report, or no owner with an email.

sent.description: One entry per person emailed, with how many of their items end within the window.

skipped.description: Tenants left alone: not active, or with nothing new to remind anyone about.

now.description:
Epoch milliseconds to treat as now, for tests and backfills. By default each collection is
judged by the clock its writer uses: the authentication clock for sessions, devices,
relationships, the outbox, and audit hooks, and the wall clock for OAuth, SAML, and SSF records.

batchSize.description: Records read per transaction (default 500, 1-5000). Short transactions keep the write lock brief.

limit.description: The most records one run deletes (default 10000, at most 1000000); see `truncated`.

deliveryRetentionMs.description:
How long delivered and abandoned deliveries stay (outbox email, SMS, and webhook history, failed
Shared Signals deliveries): default 30 days, 0-3650 days. Pending deliveries are never swept.

graceMs.description: A margin past expiry before a record is deleted, against clock skew between instances (default 5 minutes, at most 1 day).

deleted.description: Records deleted per collection; collections with nothing to delete are omitted.

truncated.description: The run stopped at `limit` before finishing; more records may be due, so run it again.

code.description: Stable error code, for example ACCESS_DENIED.

message.description: Human-readable explanation; may change between releases.
